In Al-Adsani v. United Kingdom (2001), the Grand Chamber held by 9–8 that the UK's grant of state immunity to Kuwait did not violate Article 6. The Court treated immunity as a proportionate limit on access to court. So it found immunity and the fair-trial right not in conflict, which is option C. Option B describes the same result less accurately, since the Court did not rank immunity above the right but found no violation.

CONFIDENCE: 66
